## `pivot_longer()`

Data stored in wide format are easier for humans to read and process, but to perform data analysis, wide-format data need to be converted to long (tidy) format. This can be done by using the `pivot_longer()` function.

```r
pivot_longer(
  .data,
  cols,
  ...,
  names_to = 'name',
  names_prefix = 'NULL',
  names_sep = 'NULL',
  values_to = 'value',
  values_drop_na = FALSE
)
```

:::{.callout-note icon='false'}
## Example 1.

Convert the `patients_data` dataset from wide to long format. The data records the blood pressure of five patients at three different visits.

```{r}
patient_data <- tibble(
  patient_id = c("P001", "P002", "P003", "P004", "P005"),
  age = c(45, 62, 37, 54, 48),
  visit1 = c(128, 142, 118, 135, 126),
  visit2 = c(124, 138, 121, 132, 123),
  visit3 = c(122, 134, 116, 129, 120)
)

patient_data
```

## `pivot_wider()`

Data stored in long format are useful for data analysis, but sometimes we want to reorganize the data so that each observation occupies a single row and different variables occupy separate columns. The `pivot_wider()` function converts data from long format to wide format.

```r
  pivot_wider(
    data,
    id_cols = NULL,
    names_from,
    values_from,
    ...
  )
```
